1#main: Which kilayim is d'oraisa and which is d'rabbanan. In it are 7 seifim. Once wool joined with linen, if there is a side of joining in the world, it is forbidden because of shaatnez. How so? Wool and linen that were mixed together and combed them, and made felt from them; or mixed and spun them together and wove a garment from that spinning; or sewed a wool garment with a linen one—even if he sewed them with silk or hemp threads; or sewed a wool garment with linen threads or a linen garment with wool threads; or tied wool threads with linen threads or braided them—this is shaatnez.
2#main: A wool garment that he joined with a linen garment in one insertion (meaning: one thrust of the needle into the garment)—this is not a joining and is not shaatnez. If he gathered both ends of the thread as one, or inserted two insertions—this is shaatnez. (And some say it is not shaatnez except with two insertions and tying both ends of the thread) (Tur in the name of the Rosh).
3#main: A wool garment that tore—it is permitted to join it with linen threads and tie it, but not to sew it. {Rama: And likewise it is permitted to place wool in a linen pillow or cushion even though all around it is sewn and one cannot remove the wool—it is like a linen sack filled with wool whose mouth is sewn, for there is no shaatnez in this (so is in the Tur). And even if the sewing is with wool itself, it is permitted, for one can take the wool from there without undoing the sewing. But in wool garments of shaatnez, it is forbidden in such a case, for one cannot take the garments from there without undoing the sewing (own reasoning, and Mordechai chapter BaMah Ishah and Tosafot first chapter of Beitzah). And likewise it is permitted to join wool sleeve-houses that have knots or buttons in linen sleeve-houses that have holes and insert the knots or buttons into the holes, since they are loose and one can remove them with one's finger without tearing the holes—even if one leaves them thus always. But if they are so stuck that one cannot remove them without tearing the holes, it is a joining and forbidden (Terumat HaDeshen siman 256).}
4#main: It is permitted to wear a wool shirt over a linen shirt and tie them together, even if one cannot remove them without undoing the tie—even if it is a permanent knot, provided he not join them to one another with sewing in two insertions. And some forbid a permanent knot. {Rama: And it appears to me that those sleeve-houses made in these lands called portekhi—that is, made of wool and have a band passing through them back and forth like a strap in the passage of tefillin—are permitted even if the band is linen or the reverse, since the band can be removed without undoing the sewing; it is only like girding with a linen band over a wool shirt, and even if he ties the band when wearing them it is not called a permanent knot. But if he makes knots at both ends of the band, it appears forbidden, for one cannot remove it from there (all the reasoning of the Rav). Some say it is forbidden to wear two sleeve-houses, one of linen and one of wool, one over the other (Hagahos Ashiri, first chapter of Beitzah), for one cannot remove the lower without the upper—it is like a joining and not comparable to two shirts one over the other, where one can remove the lower without the upper (so the reason was found in Or Zarua). It is proper to be careful (°).}
5#main: One strap of wool and the other of linen—it is forbidden to gird with it, even if a leather strap is in the middle, because he ties both ends together when girding with it. But if in its middle there is wool in one place and linen in another and they are not adjacent to one another, it is permitted. And according to this, it is permitted to attach hides sewn with linen beneath wool garments, even though it is possible to insert the hemp thread of the sewing that joins the hide with the garment into a thread of the sewing of the hide (R' Yerucham and Terumat HaDeshen siman 297). And for the Rambam, all this is shaatnez d'oraisa—even if he placed wool and linen in a sack or box and rolled them, it is shaatnez d'oraisa. (And the custom follows the first view) (Tur, and likewise Ramban and Rashba siman 300 and Terumat HaDeshen there).
6#main: One who leads animals and inserts ropes into its legs, some of linen and some of wool—this is permitted even though he wraps them on its leg. But if he tied them all, they become shaatnez and it is forbidden to wrap them on its leg. (And some permit, since he does not intend to) (Hagahos Ashiri and Rabbenu Yerucham, Netiv 59) (and see below siman 301).
7#main: A sack and a box combine for shaatnez. {Rama: And likewise father and son combine for shaatnez—how so? There was a piece of wool in one of them and a piece of linen in the other, and he sewed them together—it is shaatnez (Tur).}
